assumptions.note: 1% Prop 13 base + voter-approved debt ~0.16-0.18% (unverified: no SF Treasurer page could be retrieved this session; replace with the FY2025-26 secured rate).

Derived: Social Value Bank 'talks to neighbours regularly' ~GBP 4,511/person-yr divided by an assumed ~5 local weak ties, converted to USD. Upper anchor: UK DCMS severe loneliness GBP 9,537/yr (https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/963077/Loneliness_monetisation_report_V2.pdf). Wellbeing valuations are not market values; show as adjustable.
Small value per positive chance encounter; no literature value. Sandstrom & Dunn 2014 show weak-tie interactions raise same-day wellbeing but not in $.
Weekdays modeled per year (52x5 minus holidays).
Share of a business's revenue gain that is new to the city rather than shifted from elsewhere. Literature (Volker & Handy 2021) notes most local gains are partly redistribution; no measured value.
Assessed value of new floor area (~$465/sqft). Downtown office values have collapsed (e.g. 350 California sold ~-75%, see literature/office-to-residential-conversion.md); keep as slider.
share of street traffic not modeled as agents (taxis/TNC, freight, buses, other through traffic); calibrated to counts when available
surface through-trips crossing the area between inlets
extra minutes for a through-trip to avoid the area entirely

Which car inlets drivers from each home region can use, and the extra outside-the-map minutes of each option versus the region's main route (the legacy inlet, 0). Drivers pick the cheapest inlet by route cost, so closures shift entry points. Directions follow the regional freeway network (Bay Bridge -> I-80 ramps and the Embarcadero/SoMa grid; US-101/I-280 -> the south edge; western SF -> Market/Mission and the west edge; North Beach/Marin -> Broadway/Columbus and the north edge). Minutes are judgment, not measured.

Extra perceived minutes for entering or leaving the map on a lower-class street (slower approach outside the map, more signals). Keeps drivers on arterials unless a closure makes a side street clearly shorter.

Through-traffic only uses non-freeway inlets whose class penalty is at most this (primary/secondary/tertiary). Freeway-to-freeway traffic stays on the freeway and never enters the street grid. Through volume between map sides is weighted by the lane capacity of each side's eligible inlets.
replanning days for the baseline
replanning days for a plan (warm-started from baseline)
congestion smoothing between replanning days

No published work-trip mode split for FiDi-only workplaces was retrievable. Anchors: (1) ACS 2024 B08601, people WORKING in SF County, commuters excl. WFH: drive alone 42.1%, carpool 8.5%, transit 34.2%, walk 8.6%, bike 3.3%, other 3.4%; WFH 15.9% of workers. (2) SFCTA Downtown Travel Study (2023, all trip purposes, downtown): auto 36.9%, transit 20.9%, walk/bike 39.7%, TNC 2.5% (https://www.sfcta.org/sites/default/files/2025-05/Downtown_Travel_Study_FINAL_Report_2025-05-22_Executive_Summary.pdf). FiDi is far more transit-oriented than the county (BART/Muni Metro trunk, $22-40/day parking), so we shift ~16 pts from car to transit/walk. Commute-share values exclude WFH and sum to 1.0; wfh is separate. Sensitivity: use the ACS county split as the car-heavy bound.

Anchor: 76.3% of SF-resident workers have >=1 vehicle (B08014: 109,361 of 460,929 have none). No ACS table crosses vehicles by worker earnings; gradient by tier is assumed. Note ACS B08519 (SF workplace) shows auto commute share is nearly flat by earnings (~49% <$15k, ~52% $15-50k, ~50% >=$50k of non-WFH commuters), so income mainly matters through VOT, not car access.
Urban cycling ~15 km/h incl. signals (common planning assumption; no SF measurement retrieved).
perceived-distance discount for cycling on car-free streets; v1 used 0.25 and overshot Market St cycling (+530% vs +25%), revised to the ~10-15% detour cyclists accept for calmer routes
perceived-distance factor for cycling on primary/secondary streets with traffic
perceived-distance discount for walking on car-free streets; v1 used 0.30 and overshot footfall (+91% vs +29%), revised to the ~10% detour pedestrians accept for pleasant routes
travel-time factor on Market St for private cars before 2020: forced turns at 10th, 6th and 3rd made through-driving impractical (SFMTA 2009/2015 restrictions)
lognormal sd of perceived edge cost across cyclists (stochastic route choice, 3 draws)
share of Muni's Market St running time exposed to car congestion (red transit-only lanes cover most of Market); v1 used 0.5
share of non-office workers present on a weekday
Civic/institutional/PDR density; no SF-specific value retrieved.
shoppers/tourists entering the area on a weekday
people coming into the area for dinner/drinks on a weekday evening
agent budget; sets people-per-agent scale
66% daily coffee drinkers x ~29% buying away from home => ~19% of adults/day (derived); bumped for downtown office commuters (assumed).
Office workers buying coffee right after arriving; no SF measurement.
share of passers-by who stop in (walkers only); calibrated so walkers visit ~2x as often as drivers
Huff/MNL distance decay for walking destination choice
utility bonus for POIs fronting a car-free street (pleasantness, outdoor seating); v1 used 0.35
CNS Bluetooth scans every 5 min. We use 15-min co-presence bins at places/segments for compute reasons (assumed).

No direct measurement exists. Calibrate so that light-traffic vs heavy-traffic streets reproduce Appleyard's ~2-3x gap in local acquaintances (literature/social-interaction-in-public-space.md). Hall 2019 (https://greatergood.berkeley.edu/article/item/how_long_does_it_take_to_make_a_friend).
Days a habitual lunch-spot pairing repeats per year (hybrid work ~2-3 office days/week).
Times/Herald Sq: +84% people staying; Oslo +43% staying. Absolute share lingering is assumed.
